name: Güenoa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Charruan; only Hervas 1787 catechism text fragment exists, no phonological description

sources.note: Says Güenoa is known only from the Hervás catechism; cites Viegas Barros 2012 'Breves apuntes sobre fonología comparativa de las lenguas de la familia Charrúa' (XIII Congreso SAL) as the comparative phonology of the family — not opened (see list of works to obtain).

sources.citation: Lafone Quevedo, Samuel A. 1897. Los indios chanases y su lengua, con apuntes sobre los querandíes, timbúes, yaros, boanes, guenoas o minuanes, y un mapa étnico. Boletín del Instituto Geográfico Argentino XVIII: 115-154.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section V on the Yaros/Boanes/Güenoas-Minuanes (pp. 129-130) is ethnohistorical (Techo, Lozano, Hervás Catálogo I:166,187). The one stress sentence in the article, 'No tenían versificación y el acento se cargaba sobre la penúltima sílaba' (p. 139), is Larrañaga's rule 7 for Chaná, not Güenoa.

sources.citation: Hervás y Panduro, Lorenzo. 1787. Saggio pratico delle lingue (Idea dell'Universo XXI). Cesena: Gregorio Biasini. No. 308 'Lingua Guenoa', Art. VI, pp. 228-229.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The sole primary record of Güenoa: a ~20-line catechism dialogue with literal Italian gloss, no grammatical notes, no accent marks on the Güenoa words (unlike the Italian gloss), nothing whatsoever on pronunciation or stress. For neighbouring Zamuca Hervás says he lacked 'elementi gramaticali'; for Güenoa he gives none either.

sources.citation: Hervás y Panduro, Lorenzo. 1787. Vocabolario poligloto (Idea dell'Universo XX). Cesena.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Güenoa entry at all (a full-text search for stress/accent the full scanned).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page guen1235 and reference records 13948, 308497, 38210, 320602
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive references for Güenoa; only Hervás 1787 (overview;text), Vignati 1940 (minimal) and Lafone Quevedo 1897 (wordlist, Chaná) are attached. All three were opened above.

sources.citation: Jaime, Blas W. Omar & J. Pedro Viegas Barros. 2013. La lengua chaná: patrimonio cultural de Entre Ríos. Paraná: Editorial de Entre Ríos.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Its §4 'Acento' (stress on one of the last two syllables, usually final) is about Chaná. Güenoa appears only as catechism forms (<detit>, <hallen>, <guarete>, <yu(t)>, 'hum') cited for lexical comparison, credited to 'Viegas Barros 2009'; no Güenoa stress statement.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. with Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: CUP. (Charruan section, ch. 4.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100.A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l); only the abstract or a snippet was reachable when a reader tried
sources.harvard_location: Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100 .A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l
sources.note: Standard handbook summary of Charruan documentation; would confirm second-hand that nothing beyond the catechism exists for Güenoa.

sources.citation: Vignati, Milcíades Alejo. 1940. El catecismo Güenoa del Abate Hervás: reproducción facsimilar. Notas del Museo de La Plata V, Antropología 18: 41-43 + 2 plates.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Facsimile of Saggio pp. 228-229 plus a 3-page bibliographic note (Outes 1913 transcription, Serrano's Kaingang comparison, Loukotka 1935 classification). Nothing on pronunciation or stress; plates confirm the original Güenoa text carries no accent marks.

sources.citation: Serrano, Antonio. 1936. Etnografía de la antigua provincia del Uruguay. Paraná.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reprints the ten Güenoa words (from Outes) in a Chaná/Güenoa/Minuán-Charrúa table and compares them with Kaingang; no stress statement for Güenoa (its only 'vocal acentuada' remark, p. 140, concerns Guaraní dialects). Prints 'rambuí' with an accent absent from Hervás's original — his own reading, not a rule.

sources.citation: Hervás y Panduro, Lorenzo. 1800. Catálogo de las lenguas de las naciones conocidas, vol. I: Lenguas y naciones americanas. Madrid. pp. 194-197.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Names the Güenoa nation and its 'dialects' (Yaro, Minuane, Bohane, Charrúa) and Camaño's 'brevísimo catecismo'; Hervás states he found no one who could inform him about the character of the language. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 2012. Breves apuntes sobre fonología comparativa de las lenguas de la familia Charrúa. Paper, XIII Congreso de la Sociedad Argentina de Lingüística, San Luis, 27-30 March 2012.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only comparative phonology of the Charruan family; the one place a modern linguist might comment on Güenoa segmental/prosodic reconstruction (but its Güenoa input is the same accent-less catechism, so a stress statement is unlikely). Cited on Wikipedia; not located online.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 2009. [work cited as 'Viegas Barros 2009' in Jaime & Viegas Barros 2013 for the Güenoa catechism forms; title not recoverable from the scanned bibliography]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The modern philological reading of the Güenoa catechism (forms like <hallen> 'muerto', <detit> 'tres'); could carry remarks on orthography/prosody. Title and venue unconfirmed.

sources.citation: Rona, José Pedro. 1964. Nuevos elementos acerca de la lengua charrúa. Montevideo: Universidad de la República.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Main 20th-century study of Charrúa proper (a sister variety, char1238 family); might discuss family-level prosody, but not Güenoa itself.

sources.citation: Outes, Félix F. 1913. Sobre las lenguas indígenas rioplatenses: materiales para su estudio. Revista de la Universidad de Buenos Aires XXIV: 232ff.

sources.note: First transcription and lexical analysis of the Güenoa catechism with Chaná comparisons (per Vignati 1940); public domain but not found on archive.org, and HathiTrust is could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Sábat Pebet, Juan Carlos & José Joaquín Figueira. [n.d., cited on Wikipedia] Compilation of all terms known of the Uruguayan aboriginal languages (Charrúa, Chaná, Güenoa).
